source.quote: Aune's own manual for the X5s 8th Anniversary Edition, read 2026-11-25; its product page's specification block is images only. This device plays from its own storage and its coaxial, optical and AES sockets are OUTPUTS. Verbatim under « Specifications »: « Input: SD card (exFAT) / USB flash drive / portable hard drive (exFAT, maximum 2TB) », « Digital output: Coaxial / Optical / AES », « Line output: RCA ». The only digital audio input is Bluetooth reception: « Bluetooth receiver: 24bit/48kHz » against « Bluetooth transmitter: 24bit/192kHz ». What it plays from storage: « WAV: 16bit | 24bit | 32bit - 44.1k / 48k / 88.2k / 96k / 176.4k / 192k / 384k », « FLAC: 16bit | 24bit | 32bit - ... 384k », « DSD: DSF / DFF DSD64-256 / SACD-ISO », « APE: 16bit / 44.1k extraHigh ». A footnote beside the same column says « To play DSD512, a high speed SD card is needed. » No converter part number; named instead are « the freescale 600M processor, the hardware decoding system, the fourth generation FPGA asynchronous technology » and « the CSR8675 Bluetooth 5.0 module ». A « Filter mode » setting appears in the manual's screenshots as « Filter mode  Slow SD » with no list anywhere.

facts.chip: None is named. The manual credits « the freescale 600M processor, the hardware decoding system, the fourth generation FPGA asynchronous technology » and a « CSR8675 Bluetooth 5.0 module » - none of which is a converter part number.

_conditions_une_clause_existe_mais_elle_: Measured 2026-11-25, and the scope decides it. On en.auneaudio.com, where the products and the manuals are, NO terms page exists: the footer carries no legal link and /terms, /privacy, /legal, /about and their /page/ variants all 404. Footer: « (c) 2026 Aune Audio. All rights reserved. » with two Chinese filing numbers. On www.auneaudio.com, the maker's Chinese single-page site, there IS a reuse-forbidding clause - « You may not reproduce, modify, distribute, or otherwise use these contents without our explicit written permission » - but its own preamble scopes it: « Welcome to the Aune Control App [...] This service agreement [...] regarding the use of the App », and the clause's subject is « The App and all its content ». The privacy page is App-scoped too. So this is the Shanling shape inverted - an application agreement instead of a store's - and the product host publishes nothing. Records are written because nothing forbidding covers the pages they cite, and the App clause is recorded here so a reader can take the stricter view if they disagree.
_tous_les_blocs_de_specifications_des_pa: Checked on the S18 EVO, S9c Pro, Yuki, Yuki SE, X1s GT, X5s 8th, S10N/S10 Pro, ARU1 and X8 XVIII: each page's `specs_html` field contains nothing but img tags. No number was read off any of them; every figure here comes from the text of the maker's own manual PDF, linked from en.auneaudio.com/downloads.
_les_PDF_dAune_perdent_leurs_espaces_ent: An extraction fact that changes how these quotes look. Aune's PDFs lose most inter-word spaces in extraction - « UserManual », « upto32bit/768k » - and they are quoted EXACTLY as extracted, with no space put back by hand. Sanity checks passed on « Specifications », « Bluetooth » and « filter ». In the S18 EVO manual the ffi ligature is dropped, « aune's o cial website » where the document reads official, and that too is left as extracted. Third distinct extraction failure met today, after pdftotext -layout eating every « t » in Shanling's manuals and a Type-1C font with no Unicode map making VMV's English tables unreadable.
_le_mot_NOS_napparait_sur_aucune_page_ni: So the non-oversampling against New-Old-Stock ambiguity never arose for this maker, and no Aune model in the current range is described as having a valve output stage. No model claims an oversampling-bypass or a filter-OFF position either: every filter menu here is a choice among filters, never a way to leave them out. `correctable` is written on no Aune record.
_son_port_USB_est_un_LECTEUR_et_ses_pris: « Input: SD card (exFAT) / USB flash drive / portable hard drive » and « Digital output: Coaxial / Optical / AES ». So the USB is storage, not audio and not charging, and the three digital sockets point outward. The ONLY digital audio input on this device is its Bluetooth receiver, at « 24bit/48kHz » - and note the transmitter is rated four times higher, « 24bit/192kHz », which is the opposite direction and not an input. A harvester reading « Coaxial / Optical / AES » plus « 384k » would have produced three high-rate inputs that do not exist.
_le_DSD_est_donne_DEUX_FOIS_avec_deux_va: « DSD: DSF / DFF DSD64-256 / SACD-ISO » in the supported-formats list, and a footnote beside the same Specifications column: « To play DSD512, a high speed SD card is needed. Please contact sales@auneaudio.com for more info. » DSD256 and DSD512 on one page, unreconciled, and the second conditioned on the card. `dsd_max` is ABSENT on this record - the maker published two answers and the higher one depends on hardware the buyer supplies.
_les_chiffres_de_lecture_ne_sont_PAS_des: The WAV, FLAC, DSD and APE rates describe files read off a card. `pcm_max_hz` records what the device converts, which is true either way, and `inputs` holds only the Bluetooth receiver. The THD+N rows printed under « Digital Output: » are measurement conditions for that output, not input ceilings.
